items.title: The first GIF ever made was a picture of an airplane — Stephen Wilhite told the New York Times in 2013 that he 'saw the format I wanted in my head and then I started programming', and insisted the pronunciation was a soft G, like Jif peanut butter
items.snippet: The Graphics Interchange Format was quietly released by CompuServe in June 1987 to solve a mundane problem: sending pictures over slow modems. Its creator, Stephen Wilhite, spent decades correcting people about how to say its name.
